🇲🇽🚆 <u>40 BILLION PESOS, 45 NEW TRAINS — AND THE FARE STAYS AT 5 PESOS</u>

Clara Brugada announced a 40-billion-peso overhaul of Mexico City's Metro Line 3: 45 new trains, full rail replacement, and modernized signaling on a line that moves over 173 million riders a year. The fare holds at 5 pesos. "Step by step, line by line, train by train," she said. Priority works begin in 2027, with no station closures this year.

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES GET THE FUNDS DIRECTLY — NO BROKERS</u>

At the Mazahua ceremonial center in San Felipe del Progreso, Sheinbaum handed indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities direct-access cards to run their own infrastructure money (FAISPIAM) — water, drainage, electrification, roads, decided in assembly. "This mechanism lets the communities administer the resources directly," she said.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>CONTRACTOR FAKED SAT, IMSS AND INFONAVIT PAPERS — BANNED</u>

Galmar Proyectos Integrales forged tax and social-security documents from SAT, IMSS and Infonavit to land a direct-award contract at the National Institute of Cardiology. Raquel Buenrostro's anti-corruption secretariat barred the firm from all federal contracting, fined it 171,973 pesos, and entered it in the sanctioned-suppliers registry.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ICE FORCED TO SUSPEND ITS ROADSIDE MANHUNT</u>

After ICE agents shot and killed two migrants in Texas and Maine, the agency suspended the traffic-stop "controls" — the roving patrols Trump ordered. Mexico counts 17 of its nationals dead in US detention and deportation operations since Trump returned. Sheinbaum's response: "Everything done to promote a human rights policy is good." Trump is already demanding the checkpoints resume.

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICO RATES ITS OWN LIFE AN 8.62 OUT OF 10 — AND RISING</u>

INEGI's 2025 well-being survey (ENBIARE) puts Mexicans' life satisfaction at 8.62 out of 10, up from 8.45 in 2021. The UN's 2026 World Happiness Report ranks Mexico 12th worldwide — and every country ahead of it is a fraction of Mexico's 133 million people. "By population size, the happiest in the world," Sheinbaum said.

🌐🐉🇲🇽 China–Latin America trade just hit a record. The region is voting with its exports.

Bilateral trade reached US$549 billion in 2025 — an all-time high — and kept climbing: US$247.3 billion in the first five months of 2026 alone, up 17.6% year over year. The figure Washington will like least: Chinese purchases FROM Latin America jumped 27.6% to US$120 billion. At the 12th China–CELAC infrastructure forum, Beijing added visa-free entry for Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Uruguay.

This is what a multipolar world looks like in a spreadsheet. While the US threatens tariffs and demands the region pick a side, Latin America is quietly multiplying its customers. Diversification here isn't ideology — it's arithmetic.

Mexico has played it cautious — tariffs on China, betting everything on the T-MEC. But the regional current is hard to miss: the neighbors who diversified are the ones negotiating with leverage. Sovereignty, in the end, is simply having somewhere else to sell.

🇲🇽🐉🔥 Mexico slapped up to 50% tariffs on China. Chinese imports rose anyway.

The numbers just came in: Chinese imports climbed 5.23% to US$42.85 billion in the first four months of 2026 — even after Mexico imposed duties of 35% to 50% across 1,463 product lines from countries without a trade deal. A roughly 15% appreciation of the peso quietly swallowed the tariffs, and Banamex says that's exactly why no generalized jump in consumer prices ever showed up.

Read it as what it always was: a signal, not a wall. The tariffs told Washington — ahead of the T-MEC review — that Mexico would "police" the supposed back door, while trade with its No. 2 partner kept flowing. China stayed China. The market routed around the politics.

That's the sovereignty lesson. When the empire demands you wall off your second-largest supplier, you can write the rule and still let a strong peso protect your own consumers. Diversification isn't obedience — it's keeping the door open on your own terms.
